page: Google Cloud Platform c4a-standard-4-lssd is an arm64-based virtual machine instance belonging to the c4a server family. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs and 16.0 GB of system memory, yielding a balanced memory-to-core ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. The instance configuration includes local NVMe SSD storage, providing low-latency local disk access, and does not include any complimentary public IPv4 addresses or GPU accelerators.

Operating on the arm64 architecture, this instance is designed for workloads that benefit from modern energy-efficient instruction sets. The dedicated CPU allocation ensures consistent processing performance without resource contention from neighboring tenants. Qualitatively, the arm64 architecture combined with a balanced resource profile offers a cost-efficient alternative to traditional x86 instances for general-purpose workloads. This server type is suitable for web serving, application servers, containerized microservices, and lightweight database workloads that require local scratch space.
description: The Google Cloud Platform c4a-standard-4-lssd is an arm64-based virtual machine instance from the c4a family, configured with 4 dedicated vCPUs and 16.0 GB of system memory. This configuration establishes a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, providing 4.0 GB of memory per core. The instance features integrated local NVMe SSD storage to support high-speed local read and write operations, though it lacks dedicated GPU hardware and complimentary public IPv4 addresses. Built on a dedicated CPU allocation model, it delivers predictable performance for general-purpose applications. The arm64 architecture offers a resource-dense and cost-efficient profile for modern cloud deployments. It is well-suited for workloads such as web serving, containerized microservices, development environments, and database tasks requiring local scratch storage.
